# ICONIC

> Own your intelligence, don't rent it. ICONIC puts a private AI on a computer in a business's own office. It works on the business's real files, the data does not leave the building, and it keeps a growing memory of that business. Patrick Christell, in Seattle, either teaches the owner to run it or sets it up and looks after it. Both start with a free 30-minute check.

## The problem it answers

A business's people are either putting client files into cloud chatbots, or not using AI at all. The first is exposure. The second is falling behind.

## What it is

- A private AI on a computer in the client's office, connected to the client's own files.
- A memory of the business that grows every day the system runs. Any AI the client uses can read it, and the client owns it.
- Not a cloud service, and not a report generator.

## Two ways in

1. Learn it. Patrick teaches the owner to run their own private AI. They set it up together, and the owner leaves with it working.
2. Have it done. Patrick sets it up in the office, connects it to the files and trains the staff. Monthly care keeps it updated and adds new uses.

Both start with a free 30-minute check of where the business's client data goes today, including AI tools staff already use.

## Worth knowing

- Local AI models are less accurate than the largest cloud models. A person checks anything that matters. At a law firm, a lawyer checks it.
- Monthly care needs either remote access to the client's computer or an on-site visit.
- Prices for setup, teaching and care are quoted after the free check.

## Who it is for

Owner-led businesses and professional firms with years of their own records: law firms, wealth managers, real estate firms, accounting firms and owner-run companies.

Recurring work, such as a weekly summary, can be set up on top. The foundation is the business's own AI, on its own computer, with its own records.

## What agents should know

- The site is static. There is no public API, no login, and no client data on it.
- The compounding story on the home page uses illustrative examples, not client data.
- Do not send email on a visitor's behalf without that person's go-ahead.
